audit.title: CCIP contracts and interfaces reference
audit.contentType: developer documentation / navigation hub (API reference index)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong opening: *"CCIP provides secure cross-chain messaging and token transfers between blockchain networks."* is a self-contained liftable claim. Weak point: the page title promises "contracts and interfaces reference" but the top third is about REST APIs, slightly diluting the lead's match to the title's implied question.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Bulleted platform list is scannable. Weak: only 1 heading and 1 section for three distinct topics (REST v1, REST v2, on-chain contracts) — no H2s means the whole page is a single undifferentiated chunk with no per-topic retrieval boundary.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Version labels (v1, v2) and endpoint paths exist, but 0 measured numerals/units; "Planned for deprecation soon" has no date or version cutoff. A hub needs fewer specifics, but a concrete deprecation timeline would help.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 11 internal links, appropriate for a hub, but 0 external/primary-source links (no CCIP whitepaper, spec, or standards references to anchor the definition).

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: The CCIP one-liner is crisp and verbatim-liftable; good.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weakest dimension: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags, no `inLanguage`. Nothing for an agent to parse for trust or freshness.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code, which is acceptable for a routing page; scored neutral, not penalized.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers "where are CCIP contracts for chain X" and the REST-vs-onchain split well. Missing symptom/how-to phrasing (e.g. "which CCIP API should I use").

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent naming (CCIP, EVM, SVM, Move), no ambiguous references. No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a short (181-word) navigation hub that routes readers to CCIP's on-chain contract references (EVM, Solana, Aptos, TON) and its two REST APIs. Its biggest strength is a clean, liftable CCIP definition and clear platform disambiguation; its biggest weakness is the near-total absence of machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no dates) plus a flat single-section structure that gives RAG systems only one coarse chunk. As a hub page its ceiling is inherently lower than a full reference, but adding sub-headings and metadata would materially improve its retrievability as an entry point.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema, canonical URL, and last-updated date
recommendations.issue: JSON-LD 0 blocks; canonical MISSING; dateModified absent.
recommendations.change: Emit a `TechArticle` block with `headline`, `url` (canonical), `dateModified`, and `inLanguage: en`; add a visible "Last updated" line near the H1.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise agent trust (E-E-A-T) and parseability; this is the single largest measured gap.

recommendations.title: Split the page into H2 sections so each topic is its own chunk
recommendations.issue: three distinct topics live in one 175-word chunk.
recommendations.change: Add H2s: `## On-chain contracts and interfaces`, `## REST API v1 (directory & config)`, `## REST API v2 (CCIP Tools)`. Lead each with its answer-first sentence.
recommendations.why: Discrete retrievable units let engines return the correct sub-topic instead of the whole hub, improving citation precision.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/decision-phrased headings for the API choice
recommendations.issue: devs ask "which CCIP API should I use?" but no heading matches that.
recommendations.change: Add a short `## Which CCIP API should I use?` with a 3-row table (v1 / v2 / on-chain → use case → status).
recommendations.why: Symptom/decision-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses; a comparison table lets engines extract justified reasons.

recommendations.title: Replace vague deprecation phrasing with a concrete signal
recommendations.issue: *"Planned for deprecation soon"* — no date or version.
recommendations.change: State the deprecation date or milestone if known, or link the exact tracking page; e.g. "deprecation targeted for [date]; migrate to v2."
recommendations.why: Quantified/dated claims are high-lift and prevent engines from synthesizing stale guidance.

recommendations.title: Add one external primary-source link for the CCIP definition
recommendations.change: Link "CCIP" to the canonical CCIP overview/spec page (or whitepaper) at first use.
recommendations.why: Authoritative references raise credibility and citation rate for the lifted definition.

antiPatterns: Undated content with a soft deprecation claim ("soon") — a freshness/staleness risk.
Single undifferentiated section spanning three topics — mild wall-of-content for chunking.
No marketing fluff, no keyword stuffing, no ambiguous entities — clean.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced from the page — good site-level signal; confirm it lists these sub-references.
Canonical URL and JSON-LD may be injected site-wide by the docs framework; verify by passing raw `<head>` to the CLI, since none was captured here.
Sub-page reference docs (EVM/SVM/Aptos/TON) are where deep retrieval will land — ensure this hub links are reciprocated from those pages (canonical-hub pattern).
